hypothesis.count_consequence: Count-neutral. Both sites are 2-for-2 instruction replacements (add/lwz against addi/lwzx); the streams are already T167/O167 and no cure on this axis changes that.
hypothesis.screened_against_target: yes -- both sites were read in the aligned view (`fnasm game/audio/audio AudioLoadPart 0xb0:0xd8 --diff` and the +0x64 cluster in --ops) and both reproduce verbatim under every spelling tried. NOT screened: no sibling function in the TU has been checked, which is exactly what the hypothesis asks for.
hypothesis.statement: The two addressing sites (+0x64 in the queue-slot scan and +0xc4 in the partRomBank load) show the SAME asymmetry in the SAME direction -- the target materialises (base+index) into a register and folds the constant into the load displacement, while ours materialises (index+constant) and uses an indexed load -- and five distinct source spellings across three records cannot move either one. A systematic, whole-function, source-immune direction like that is the signature of a cflag or compiler-variant difference rather than a source form, so the next lane should census the same `add`+`lwz` vs `addi`+`lwzx` shape across every NonMatching function in game/audio/audio.c: if it is TU-wide the question is the TU's cflags (audio.c uses cflags_demo), and if it is confined to AudioLoadPart the compiler-variant idea is dead and the eleventh web is the only remaining lever.
